transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-10-05
Time: 14:00 PT / 17:00 ET
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Sara Villanueva (Redwood CSM); Dr. Elena Ruiz (Head of AI, Citrine), Marcus Lee (Infra Lead), Priya Singh (CISO), Jordan Park (Product)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick roll call, we're here to talk renewal and expansion for Citrine. 
[00:12] Elena: Yep, hi all, thanks for setting this up. We've been really happy with Redwood in prod, so main thing is capacity and the euro region ask.
[00:23] Marcus: Hi, Marcus here. We're seeing queue growth at peak and want to plan for a 2x uplift plus a standby pool.
[00:31] Liam: Great, thanks. Quick clarifying question: when you say 2x, is that concurrent throughput or sustained throughput?
[00:40] Marcus: Mostly concurrent RPS, sustained over 30-60 minute windows during batch processing — genomics pipelines spike.
[00:50] Jordan: We also want to add eu-west-1 to reduce latency for EU partners and for data residency reasons.
[00:57] Priya: And from security, we need to validate SOC2 artifacts, KMS integration details, and log retention — also whether Redwood Dedicated supports our HSM.
[01:08] Maya: Perfect. I'll walk through options: hosted with reserved capacity vs Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) vs Private (VPC). Each has tradeoffs on cost, isolation, and operational overhead.
[01:20] Liam: If I jump in — Dedicated gives you guaranteed pools, predictable latency and we can pin model versions. For 2x capacity and an additional region we'd recommend spinning up a dedicated pool in eu-west-1 and keep a smaller burst pool in us-west for DR.
[01:34] Elena: Is there a big latency delta between hosted and dedicated? We care about p95 under 200ms for short-form inference.
[01:42] Liam: It depends. With dedicated on the same region you'll see lower jitter and consistent p95; hosted can hit similar medians but during noisy neighbors you can see more variability. Our benchmarks show dedicated p95 ~120-150ms for your typical small LLM workloads, hosted ~160-220ms in peak. (note: these are approximations)
[02:00] Marcus: Okay, and cost? Our finance prefers to look at committed usage for a lower unit price.
[02:06] Maya: For committed 12-months with a 2x capacity commit we can provide a stepped discount — I'll send numbers after the call. There's also committed burst credits and reserved pool pricing for Dedicated.
[02:17] Elena: Does Redwood provide cross-region KV cache replication or is that something we'd manage?
[02:24] Liam: We have prefix/KV caching at the platform layer. Cross-region replication isn't automatic; you can have per-region caches and we recommend a warm cache strategy on failover. For strict DR you might replicate important prefixes via your app layer.
[02:39] Priya: About KMS/HSM: can Redwood Dedicated integrate with our BYOK HSM? Data at rest encryption — we need to map key lifecycle and key rotation.
[02:48] Liam: Yes, Dedicated and Private support customer-managed keys via our KMS integrations. HSM specifics — we support standard KMIP/HSM integrations in Private. For dedicated hosted in our managed VPC we can integrate with partner KMS — we'll confirm specifics in the security pack.
[03:03] Sara: We'll attach our SOC2 package and the KMS integration guide in the follow-up mail.
[03:09] Marcus: For the benchmark, what inputs do you need from us? Model, sequence length, concurrency patterns?
[03:16] Liam: Exactly. If you can share a representative prompt set, avg tokens, the model variant you use (we suspect you're on an Llama-derivative?), and approximate concurrency profiles we can mirror it. Also any custom ops or quantization you use.
[03:30] Elena: We're mostly on a 7B fine-tuned model, sequences median 256 tokens, peaks up to 1024 for longer runs. Concurrency peaks at ~180 RPS currently.
[03:42] Liam: Great, that helps. We'll recommend a pool sizing and batching policy. For a 2x uplift we'd suggest moving to two N nodes (config to be shared).
[03:51] Jordan: Timeline wise, we want this in place by Q1 2028. Is that feasible?
[03:57] Maya: Totally feasible — committed renewal in Oct-Nov, provisioning in Nov-Dec, validation in Jan, full rollout Q1. We'll coordinate SRE handoffs.
[04:06] Priya: A couple of security clarifications: audit logs retention window, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and do you support VPC peering?
[04:14] Liam: Audit logs: we can ship audit logs to your SIEM and set retention; retention durations depend on plan (we can extend). SSO/SAML is supported with SCIM provisioning and granular RBAC. VPC peering is supported in Private and in Dedicated via customer-managed VPC options.
[04:29] Priya: Good. Also need clarity on data deletion/retention policy for training-usage data — do you persist user prompts?
[04:36] Maya: By default hosted API stores minimal telemetry for 30 days; with an enterprise contract we can commit to custom retention and opt-out for prompt storage. We'll include language in the contract.
[04:46] Elena: On contract length, we're considering 12 months with a mid-term capacity review and a 24-month option. Any pricing differences?
[04:54] Maya: 24-months gets you better discounts but less flexibility. We'll provide 12- and 24-month tiers. Also, if you commit to a larger reserve we can include startup credits for cross-region setup.
[05:06] Marcus: For eu-west-1 provisioning, what's the lead time?
[05:11] Liam: For Dedicated pools in eu-west-1, typical lead time is 2-4 weeks once the contract and payment are processed. If you need Private VPC on-prem, that's longer — usually 6-8 weeks.
[05:22] Jordan: Any concerns with regulatory data residency rules in the EU?
[05:27] Priya: We need to ensure customer data never leaves EU for those datasets.
[05:31] Maya: We can pin region and ensure logs and storage remain in eu-west-1; we'll include region-scoping in the contract.
[05:37] Elena: About fallbacks — if eu region capacity gets saturated, can traffic failover to us region? That would violate residency, but curious about options.
[05:46] Liam: You can set policy-based routing: sensitive traffic stays in eu, non-sensitive can route to us. For strict residency we recommend Dedicated with strict routing and no cross-region fallback.
[05:57] Marcus: Ok makes sense. Back on the benchmark: we'd like to include a test for p95 and throughput and also a cost-per-token projection at your recommended config.
[06:07] Liam: We'll include p50/p95/p99 and cost breakdown. Expect a run in eu-west-1 with the same model and token distribution.
[06:15] Maya: I'll prepare a quote for a 12-month commit with 2x capacity and an add-on for the eu-west pool, plus a 24-month option. I'll also share the security pack and contract draft.
[06:25] Priya: If possible, include an SLA for p95 latency and an uptime SLA tied to credits.
[06:31] Maya: Yep — standard SLA options and premium SLA add-on will be in the contract.
[06:36] Elena: Any other operational things we should know? Rollouts, canary tests, and model pinning?
[06:42] Liam: We support canary rollouts per route, model pinning per environment, and automatic fallback to smaller models if needed. We'll give you runbooks for rollouts and A/B testing.
[06:52] Jordan: For CI/CD integration, do you have Terraform or APIs for autoscaling and pool management?
[06:58] Liam: Yes, we have APIs and Terraform provider docs. We can open a restricted API key for your infra team.
[07:05] Marcus: One last question — competitors: we were asked to benchmark vs HugeCloud AI and a self-hosted stack. Any notes or gotchas?
[07:12] Maya: HugeCloud AI gives strong regional presence but tends to be pricier for committed pools; self-hosted has lower unit costs but high ops overhead. We'll include a comparative note in the proposal.
[07:23] Elena: Sounds good. Anything else from Redwood?
[07:27] Sara: We'll attach the SOC2 summary, KMS guide, and example contract in the follow-up email. Also I'll set up the benchmark kick-off meeting once Marcus shares the prompt set.
[07:38] Maya: Ok let's recap next steps: Maya sends pricing and contract draft; Liam schedules benchmark with Marcus; Priya sends compliance doc list; Jordan confirms rollout date.
[07:50] Priya: Thanks all, we'll aim to get the compliance list to you by Monday.
[07:55] Marcus: I'll get the prompt set and concurrency logs over this week.
[07:59] Elena: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the proposal.
[08:03] Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up via email and set the benchmark in the calendar. Bye.

Post-call notes: Shared links referenced during call: pricing and region note (internal link) https://app.redwood.ai/proposals/CTN-19240 , Security pack (link) https://redwood.ai/security/soc2-pack.pdf
